top_stories.title: Microsoft Authenticator vulnerability let rogue Android apps steal work account access
top_stories.summary: A vulnerability (CVE-2026-80097) in Microsoft Authenticator for Android allowed any app on the device to silently hijack work account access by exploiting Authenticator's broker functionality. The flaw required no user interaction and no special permissions, affecting enterprise accounts accessed through apps like Teams and Outlook.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed
top_stories.summary: An attacker compromised Microsoft 365 email accounts across 79 organizations over ten weeks by replaying stolen authentication session tokens, bypassing the need for passwords entirely. The threat actor deployed hidden inbox rules to conceal their activity from victims, with findings documented by security firm Huntress.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 Token-Replay Attacks Compromise 97 Accounts at 79 Organizations
top_stories.summary: Researchers at Huntress documented a Microsoft 365 adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) campaign that captured and replayed authentication tokens to compromise 97 accounts across 79 organizations between July 14 and September 22, 2026. The attacks bypassed MFA by stealing valid session tokens after authentication, targeting email accounts through relay infrastructure.

top_stories.title: The 2% Problem: Three Vendors Built Agent-Identity Governance. Almost Nobody Is Using It.
top_stories.summary: SailPoint has reported that while 79% of enterprises run AI agents in production, only 2% have deployed agent-identity governance controls, highlighting a critical gap in non-human identity management. The article examines three vendors that have built agent-identity governance solutions, framing the low adoption rate as a significant emerging challenge for IAM professionals managing autonomous AI workloads.

top_stories.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — and Fraudsters Are Counting on It
top_stories.summary: The article covers social engineering attacks targeting help desks, where threat actors use AI-assisted impersonation to bypass identity verification and gain unauthorized access. This directly relates to IAM authentication and identity verification processes, particularly around help desk identity proofing and MFA bypass techniques.

news.title: DreamHost forces password resets in ongoing "incident"
news.summary: DreamHost forced password resets for email and FTP/SFTP users following an incident that disrupted connections to its File Manager interface. The forced reset indicates a potential credential compromise, though details about the nature of the incident have not been fully disclosed.

news.title: When an AI Agent Is the Incident, the Identity Record Is the Evidence
news.summary: A new guide from NIST, CISA, and NSA frames runaway AI agents as security incidents requiring formal response procedures. The core identity challenge identified is establishing and recording the authority under which an AI agent operated, requiring identity records to be established before an incident occurs.

news.title: Attackers Use Microsoft Teams IT Support Scams to Deploy Malware and Ransomware
news.summary: Threat actors are exploiting Microsoft Teams' external chat feature to conduct IT support impersonation scams and deliver malware and ransomware across hundreds of documented incidents. The attacks rely on throwaway tenants and social engineering rather than authentication vulnerabilities, using Teams as an initial access vector.

news.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
news.summary: An automated attack campaign is using stolen GitHub tokens to inject malicious workflows that expose repository secrets through GitHub Actions logs, affecting private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments. Security firm Wiz analyzed the campaign, which exploits compromised authentication tokens to access and exfiltrate secrets before deleting evidence of the runs.

news.title: Show HN: Frontdoor: find who can assume into your cloud accounts
news.summary: A new open-source tool called Frontdoor has been released that maps federated identity trust paths into cloud accounts across AWS, GCP, and Azure. It identifies external access vectors including OIDC, SAML, cross-account, and cross-cloud relationships using a single binary with no database requirement.

news.title: Leaked LiteLLM Master Key Let Attackers Steal GitHub Tokens and Hijack Release Pipeline
news.summary: LiteLLM disclosed that a master key accidentally committed to a public GitHub repository in late May 2026 enabled a threat actor to steal GitHub tokens and compromise the release pipeline. The attacker used the exposed credentials to push a malicious version of the LiteLLM Python package to users.

news.title: jumpserver v4.10.20
news.summary: JumpServer released version 4.10.20 of its open-source Privileged Access Management platform. The platform provides secure access to SSH, RDP, Kubernetes, Database, and RemoteApp endpoints through a web browser for DevOps and IT teams.

news.title: Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of Okta’s Oktane event
news.summary: TheCUBE's coverage of Okta's Oktane event highlighted key insights around AI agent governance and identity security. The coverage focused on how enterprises need identity controls that extend beyond initial login to govern agent actions across applications and tool delegations.

news.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
news.summary: Microsoft has launched Project Perception, which introduces Guardian Agents designed to monitor and contain anomalous AI agent behavior as a security control. Security experts are raising concerns that using AI agents to police other AI agents could introduce additional risk, particularly as autonomous agents present new insider-threat-like challenges to identity and access management frameworks.

news.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
news.summary: Hackers have breached enterprise firewalls and VPNs, including Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect devices, exposing over 70,000 credentials. The campaign targeted network edge devices across numerous organizations worldwide, with operators attempting further compromise of some victims.

news.title: Enable cross-Region fine-grained data access with AWS Lake Formation and Trusted Identity Propagation
news.summary: AWS has expanded Trusted Identity Propagation with IAM Identity Center to support cross-Region data access in AWS Lake Formation. The feature allows fine-grained access controls on Amazon S3 and Redshift data across Regions while maintaining the querying user's actual corporate identity.

news.title: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
news.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a supply chain compromise in LiteLLM version 1.107.0 that used Python startup hooks to steal credentials. The attack involved remote code loading as a mechanism for credential theft, with Microsoft providing detections and mitigations for the vulnerability.

news.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Rise as Evercore Survey Flags Strengthening Demand: Okta, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Climb 4%
news.summary: Cybersecurity stocks including Okta rose approximately 4% following an Evercore ISI quarterly survey indicating strengthening demand in the sector. The stock movement reflects broader cybersecurity market sentiment rather than Okta-specific news or IAM developments.

news.title: AGL hits half-million milestone with passkey adoption
news.summary: AGL has reached 500,000 users adopting passkeys as part of its authentication uplift initiative. The company discussed its technical stack and approach to implementing passwordless authentication at scale.

news.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
news.summary: Google, Mozilla, Apple, and the Go project blocked certificates from Indian certificate authority eMudhra after 8 private keys were found to be compromised. The nature of the key compromise remains unclear, but the swift response from major platform vendors resulted in distrust of the affected certificates across multiple ecosystems.

news.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
news.summary: A Dark Reading roundtable examined how AI is creating identity gaps in the software development lifecycle that CISOs must address. The discussion highlighted collaboration, improved identity visibility, and reduced testing costs as key strategies for managing identity security challenges in AI-driven development environments.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. The company attributed the accelerated vulnerability discovery pace to AI assistance, while security experts note organizations are struggling to keep up with testing and deploying the volume of fixes.
